units.t_min_read: electrolysis time, min, as read from the marker position
units.rate_mM_per_min: rate of production (+) or consumption (-) in mM of the species per min as plotted; N2 and N2O per molecule (see n_basis_note)
units.match_score: normalized cross-correlation (template_match) or ring-darkness score (ring_fit); low values mark overlapped markers

structure: 56 rows. Top panel (y -2 to 4 mM/min): NO2- (7 points, every 30 min) and N2 (14 points: 0, about 4 min, then every 15 min). Bottom panel (y -0.8 to 0.8 mM/min): H2N2O2, NH2OH, NH3 (7 points each, every 30 min) and N2O (14 points: 0, about 4 min, then every 15 min). The 15 min spacing of N2 and N2O matches the on-line GC sampling; the liquid species are sampled every 30 min.
extraction_method: Raster digitization of the thesis page image (reader page 216, 300 dpi) by an agent script (OpenCV). Shared x axis calibrated on the seven labelled major ticks (0 min at px 640 to 180 min at px 1898, residuals below 0.07 min); each panel's y axis calibrated separately on its own ticks (top: 4 at px 351 to -2 at px 1214, 143.8 px per mM/min; bottom: 0.8 at px 1280 to -0.8 at px 2142.5, 539 px per mM/min; residuals below 0.002 mM/min). Open squares (NO2-), filled circles (N2), filled up-triangles (NH3), open stars (N2O) and filled stars (NH2OH) located by normalized cross-correlation with templates cut from clean markers in the same figure, anchored at the geometric centre (box centre for square and circle, centroid for the triangle, circumcentre for the stars). Open circles (H2N2O2) located by a ring fit (radius 11-12 px). Markers at t = 0 are half hidden by the y axis and were matched with the right part of the template (or the right-hand arc for the circle). N2O at 120 min (upper half under the NH3 triangle) was matched with the lower half of the template. N2O at 30 min (lower part under the NH3 triangle) was matched with the full template (score 0.65). H2N2O2 at 90 min coincides with the NH3 triangle (ring-fit score 0.37, low confidence); H2N2O2, NH2OH and N2O at 180 min overlap each other. Overlay of the inverse-calibrated points on the page crop checked by eye (scratch, not committed). The thesis does not say how the rates were computed from the concentration data.
n_basis_note: Integrating the digitized rates over time (trapezoid) reproduces the concentrations of the repo dataset katsounaros2012_fig1_sn_naoh (Katsounaros et al., Electrochim. Acta 71 (2012) 270, Fig. 1, same conditions: 0.5 M NaNO3 + 1 M NaOH, -2.2 V) when N2 and N2O are counted as 2 N: cumulative N2 x 2 at 30/60/90/120/150/180 min = 20, 76, 165, 247, 290, 309 mM-N against 18, 75, 165, 249, 292, 309 in that dataset; N2O x 2 = 5, 20, 41, 55, 60, 62 against 4, 20, 42, 56, 60, 63; NH3 (x 1) = 3.6, 8.5, 14.6, 20.1, 23.9, 27.0 against 5.0, 7.6, 13.6, 19.6, 23.6, 27.6; NO2- (x 1) = 87, 117, 92, 47, 16, 6 against 107, 132, 99, 39, 10, 6. So the plotted N2 and N2O rates are per molecule, and this diagram is very probably derived from the same run as the 2012 paper's Fig. 1 (which, by the same comparison, plots N2 and N2O as N-equivalents, as that dataset's meta assumes).

checks.legend_mismatch: The caption assigns a filled down-triangle to N2, but the figure has no such marker; the only unassigned series is the filled circles in the top panel. They are taken as N2 because their maximum is at 90 min (text: N2 maximum at 90 min) and their time integral reproduces the N2 concentrations of the 2012 paper (n_basis_note).

conditions.cell: divided_batch (Teflon cell, Nafion 117 H+ form, 10 mL per compartment, platinized Pt anode, Luggin capillary), assumed from thesis ch. 5 standard setup
conditions.notes: Ambient temperature (not given numerically). Rates, not concentrations; signs as plotted (positive = production, negative = consumption).
